born.why: The previous code failed because it didn't account for items that increased n1 (bad outcomes) and blindly picked 'a2' or 'a3' based on simple thresholds, leading to death at high n1. This new code calculates ROI (health gain per cost), ignores negative ROI history, prioritizes high ROI actions, and explicitly avoids risk when health is critical (n1 > 80).

The previous code was effectively stable but vulnerable to sudden spikes in n1; this version adds a hard safety threshold at n1=90 to force a defensive action, while otherwise trusting the environment's hint (x.n5) which has maintained a safe n1 level of ~40-50.

The code primarily retains the original strategy of following the default option `x.n5` because without explicit mapping of options to outcomes for each item kind, deviating is risky; it adds a safety check at high n1 (>90) to select 'a1' (likely lower cost/risk) and prevents approaching when near death.

The code prioritizes survival by forcing a safe 'a4' action when n1 is critical (>95) or if the default choice is associated with items that historically increased n1. It aggressively selects the default option only when n1 is low (<70) and the current item kind has a proven track record of decreasing n1, otherwise falling back to 'a4' to minimize risk.
The agent prioritizes items with proven high health gain relative to cost, avoiding risky or ineffective interactions to prolong survival.

The code prioritizes keeping the agent alive by strictly avoiding actions that increase n1 (danger level), using historical data for k-specific items to validate 'a1'/'a2' safety, and defaulting to the conservative 'a4' option when history is absent or indicates risk.

The code prioritizes survival by forcing the safe option 'a4' when n1 is critical (>75) or when the current item's kind has historically increased n1, thereby avoiding known hazards and keeping n1 low.
